title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: The evaporator fan inside the freezer section has failed or is blocked.
fullDescription:
Electrolux freezers flash a 1 (sometimes as SY EF) when the evaporator fan tacho is missing. Without the fan, cold air cannot circulate and freezer temperature rises.

Causes include an iced-over fan blade, failed motor, or a broken harness. Inspect first for ice buildup around the evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the freezer for 24 hours with doors open to melt ice.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rear freezer panel and spin the fan by hand.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the evaporator fan if it is seized or noisy.

whenToCallPro: If the defrost system also shows problems or wiring needs tracing.

faq.a: Move food to another freezer; the temperature will rise quickly without airflow.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: The condenser fan on the compressor is not running.
fullDescription:
Error 5 is raised when the condenser cooling fan fails. The compressor then overheats and cycles off, causing poor cooling.

Dust buildup, a blocked blade, or motor failure are the usual causes. Pull the freezer away from the wall and inspect the rear mechanical compartment.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power before working on the rear compartment.

fixSteps.title: Clean fan
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum dust off the condenser coil and fan blade.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If fan still will not run, fit a new condenser fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If the motor runs but compressor is still overheating.

faq.a: No, the condenser is outside the freezer cabinet.

title: Defrost Heater Fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater circuit failed its self-test.
fullDescription:
Error 8 indicates the main control cannot verify current through the defrost heater. Without defrost, ice builds up on the evaporator and the freezer eventually loses cooling.

Check the heater resistance (usually 150-400 Ω) and the defrost thermostat continuity at cold temperature.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and remove freezer rear panel.

fixSteps.title: Test heater
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across the defrost heater terminals.

fixSteps.title: Replace part
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed heater or thermostat.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable with multimeter diagnostics.

faq.a: Yes, unplug 24 hours, but the error will return until the heater is fixed.

title: High Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Freezer interior has warmed above the safe threshold.
fullDescription:
HI (or H1) means the freezer has been above roughly -9 °C (15 °F) long enough to compromise food safety. It is an alarm, not a hardware fault, though it is often the symptom of one.

Check that the door has been closed, nothing blocks the vents, and no recent power loss occurred. If the alarm persists after the unit has run for several hours, investigate compressor and fan faults.

causes.cause: Door left open or not sealing

fixSteps.title: Check door
fixSteps.instruction: Close door firmly and check the gasket seals all around.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 4-6 hours to pull back down after closing.

fixSteps.title: Investigate hardware
fixSteps.instruction: If alarm persists, check fans and compressor per error codes 1, 5, and 8.

whenToCallPro: If HI persists after the freezer has run for 12 hours with a closed door.

faq.a: If the freezer was above -9 °C for more than 2 hours, discard perishable items.

title: Low Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: The freezer is colder than the control range allows.
fullDescription:
LO appears when the cabinet drops well below the setpoint, often because the damper is stuck open or the thermistor has drifted. In rare cases a stuck compressor relay causes it.

Unplug and retest after 30 minutes; if LO returns, investigate the thermistor and damper.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 10 minutes and restore power.

fixSteps.title: Check thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure freezer thermistor resistance; replace if out of spec.

whenToCallPro: If compressor cycles will not stop after thermistor replacement.

faq.q: Is food safe if LO is showing?
faq.a: Yes, food stays frozen; it just wastes energy and can freezer-burn items.

title: Thermistor Open Circuit
shortDescription: A temperature sensor reads open (no resistance reported).
fullDescription:
OP is posted when the control measures infinite resistance on a thermistor, meaning the sensor or its wiring has broken. The freezer falls back to a default run pattern that is not temperature accurate.

Inspect the sensor body and connector for damage, especially near the evaporator where ice stress is common.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove freezer rear panel to expose evaporator thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Measure
fixSteps.instruction: Check resistance; infinite means replacement needed.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new thermistor and reassemble.

whenToCallPro: If the wiring harness is damaged and requires splicing.

faq.a: No, the freezer cannot regulate without a working sensor and may over- or under-cool.

title: Thermistor Short Circuit
shortDescription: A temperature sensor is reading a short (near zero resistance).
fullDescription:
CL is the companion to OP - the sensor reads shorted instead of open. Ice damage, pinched wires, or an internal sensor fault are the common causes.

As with OP, the freezer runs on a default pattern until the sensor is fixed, which usually means excess runtime and poor temperature control.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; replace if below expected range.

whenToCallPro: If short is in an inaccessible harness inside the cabinet foam.

faq.a: Yes, in accessible areas use water-tight crimps rated for low temperatures.

title: Demo Mode Active
shortDescription: The freezer is in showroom demonstration mode and not cooling.
fullDescription:
DC indicates demo mode has been enabled, typically during retail display. In this mode the compressor never runs so food will spoil.

Exit demo mode via the control panel key combination listed in the owner manual - usually a long press of the Freezer and Alarm buttons together.

fixSteps.title: Disable demo
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold Freezer and Alarm keys for 5 seconds until DC clears.

videoSearchQuery: Electrolux freezer DC demo mode off

faq.a: Some button combinations can enable it accidentally, or the unit was shipped in demo.

title: System Communication Error
shortDescription: The display board is not receiving messages from the main control.
fullDescription:
SY is the generic communication error between the user interface and the main control board. Common triggers are a loose interconnect, moisture ingress, or a failed board on either end.

Power cycling sometimes clears it; persistent SY usually needs board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Open the door and reseat the UI harness at the top hinge.

whenToCallPro: If reseating fails and the main board is suspect.

faq.q: Will the freezer still cool with SY?
faq.a: Usually yes, the compressor runs on a default pattern, but you cannot change settings.

title: Defrost Cycle Timeout
shortDescription: The defrost cycle ran to its maximum time without terminating.
fullDescription:
DF is posted when the defrost thermostat or bimetal did not open to terminate defrost. The heater stays energised until the safety fuse opens, leaving the freezer without defrost capability.

Replace the bimetal thermostat and check the heater for damage before returning to service.

causes.cause: Open thermal fuse in heater circuit

symptoms: Water or scorch smell after defrost

fixSteps.title: Replace bimetal
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new defrost thermostat on the evaporator.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the in-line thermal fuse if open.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable working with heater circuits.

faq.a: The thermal fuse prevents overheating, but do not bypass it - replace with an identical part.
